:::{#def-cross-entropy}
#### Cross-entropy

Let $X$ be a [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) with
[probability mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) or [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) $p$,
and let $q$ be a [mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) or density on the same values.
The **cross-entropy** of $q$ relative to $p$
[@wikipedia_cross_entropy]
is the [expectation](#def-expectation), when $X$ has [distribution](random-variables.qmd#def-cdf) $p$,
of the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) (or its [continuous](#def-surprisal-continuous) form) $\surprisal_q$ measured by $q$,
where $\surprisal_q(x) \eqdef -\log q(x)$:

$$\crossentropyf{p}{q} \eqdef \E{\surprisal_q\paren{X}}.$$

We take $-\log 0 = \infty$,
so when $\P(q(X) = 0) > 0$,
the cross-entropy is infinite.

:::
